slide.text: Kano needs GIS-backed land modernization at working scale
For Kano State, land administration reform depends on field demarcation, parcel digitisation, Certificate of Occupancy generation, post-title continuity, and stronger revenue discipline.

text.p: Kano’s land-governance challenge is not only about digitizing forms. It is about moving from analogue records and fragmented field processes to a system where parcel identity, claimant evidence, legal progression, and post-title activity remain visible and controlled.

That matters because field demarcation, public display, registry verification, and ground-rent-sensitive transactions are all operationally linked. When they are disconnected, the state loses clarity, speed, and revenue visibility.

p.strong: The procurement case is therefore about building a GIS-backed workflow backbone that supports certification, discipline, and accountable growth.

tr.td: Why it matters in Kano procurement terms
Without cleaner digitisation and parcel continuity, land administration remains slow, opaque, and hard to scale.
Demarcation, evidence photography, and claimant interaction require stronger field-to-registry continuity.

td.strong: C of O generation and post-title control

tr.td: Certification, assignment, mortgage, and ground-rent-sensitive activities need clearer workflow discipline and traceability.
Kano needs stronger visibility into land-linked administrative value, post-title transactions, and the revenue potential unlocked by GIS modernization.

slide.text: For Kano, the procurement opportunity is to connect GIS, field operations, certification, and revenue-linked registry control in one working system.
